2026-TRIG-P1-B-008.subject: Maths
2026-TRIG-P1-B-008.questionText: Evaluate tan 30 deg x tan 60 deg.
2026-TRIG-P1-B-008.explanation: tan 30 deg = 1/sqrt(3) and tan 60 deg = sqrt(3). Their product is 1. Final answer: 1.
solutionSteps: tan 30 deg = 1/sqrt(3) and tan 60 deg = sqrt(3).
2026-TRIG-P1-B-008.strategyHint: Recall the standard angle table before substituting.

SAV2-026.subject: Maths
SAV2-026.questionText: A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm has a hemisphere of radius 3 cm placed on top. Find the total surface area (excluding the base of cylinder).
solutionSteps: Curved surface area of cylinder = 2πrh = 2π(3)(10) = 60π cm²
Curved surface area of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2π(3)² = 18π cm²
The top of the cylinder is covered by the hemisphere and the base is excluded, so no flat faces are added

SAV2-027.subject: Maths
SAV2-027.questionText: A cone is mounted on a hemisphere of radius 7 cm. If the slant height of cone is 10 cm, find the curved surface area of the combined solid.
solutionSteps: Curved surface area of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2π(7)² = 98π cm²
Curved surface area of cone = πrl = π(7)(10) = 70π cm²

TR3-057.subject: Maths
TR3-057.questionText: In ΔABC, D and E are points on AB and AC respectively. If AD = 3 cm, DB = 6 cm, AE = 2 cm, EC = 4 cm, is DE || BC? Justify.
TR3-057.answer: Yes, DE || BC because AD/DB = AE/EC = 1/2
solutionSteps: Since AD/DB = AE/EC, by converse of Basic Proportionality Theorem, DE || BC
TR3-057.finalAnswer: Yes, DE || BC because AD/DB = AE/EC = 1/2
